name: The Essence of Aku'Mai
label: Quest
description: Je'neu Sancrea has found the naga harvesting sapphires in Blackfathom Deeps. At Zoram'gar Outpost, the shaman asks Horde adventurers to recover them…

clips.title: The story
paras: Je'neu Sancrea has found the naga harvesting sapphires in Blackfathom Deeps. At Zoram'gar Outpost, the shaman asks Horde adventurers to recover them before their power is misused.

Je'neu Sancrea watches over the Kaldorei ruins from the Zoram Strand. Naga now mine sapphire clusters in the submerged chambers of Blackfathom Deeps, where the gems grow along damp cavern walls. Sancrea senses the serpentine invaders mean to harness their power and seeks to stop the harvest before they can use it.

The Sapphires of Aku'mai carry elemental water energy and hold clinging water spirits. Adept sorcerers could use them to fuel dangerous arcane rituals or strengthen Aku'mai, the shadowy hydra whose presence fills the subterranean temple. Recovering the clusters keeps this potent reagent from the naga and helps guard the coastline against unchecked elemental magic.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Within the beginning tunnels of Blackfathom Deeps, large sapphire clusters can be found along the cave walls. Recently it was noted that the naga were harvesting the crystals. Until it can be discerned why, I sense we should stop the naga from succeeding. The crystals have great elemental power and if used inappropriately, could make for a powerful arcane component.
Will you help me, friend? Blackfathom Deeps can be found along Zoram Strand to the north of our outpost.

clips.title: Progress
paras: How goes your search for the crystals, friend? Have you witnessed the naga harvesting them? I pray to my ancestors we find the reason they are collecting such things.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Well done, friend. These are the crystals I spoke of. Intriguing...
I can feel the power within them. The spirits of water cling to them. Whatever the naga were going to use these for... Well, let us be glad they are no longer in their hands.
